topic: Geometric Interpretation of Non-Square Matrices as Dimensional Transformations
target_audience: Undergraduate students in linear algebra or computer graphics

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: The Transformation Paradigm
lecture_lines: Square matrices reorient coordinates in the same dimension.
This transformation acts as a map for vectors.
Think of rotating a vector like a compass.
animations: 1. Display 2D grid of unit vectors (color: #FFFFFF) with a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg] in the corner for orientation.
2. Highlight i-hat (red #FF4444) and j-hat (green #44FF44).
3. Animate matrix transformation on the grid space.
4. Track i-hat and j-hat to their destination vectors.
5. Show the resulting reoriented 2D coordinate system with the updated [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg].

sections.title: Mapping Up: Embedding into Higher Dimensions
lecture_lines: Tall matrices map low dimensions into high dimensions.
This embedding injects a vector into a larger space.
A 2D shape becomes a 3D thin billboard.
animations: 1. Show 2D manifold grid embedded in 3D coordinate space [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/billboard.svg].
2. Display 3x2 matrix formula (white #FFFFFF).
3. Animate transformation mapping the 2D grid into 3D.
4. Highlight the resulting flat 2D subspace inside 3D.
5. Rotate the 3D scene to confirm 2D embedding [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/billboard.svg].

sections.title: Mapping Down: The Concept of Projection
lecture_lines: Wide matrices map high dimensions down to low.
This projection compresses data, sacrificing some depth.
Like a 3D object captured on 2D film.
animations: 1. Render 3D geometric object using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cube.svg] (color: #44CCFF).
2. Display 2x3 matrix formula (white #FFFFFF).
3. Animate projection onto a 2D plane.
4. Emphasize the loss of depth during projection.
5. Final state: flattened 2D shadow of the object represented by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cube.svg].

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Transformation Flow'
lecture_lines: Matrices bridge these differing dimensional realms.
They control expansion into higher spaces.
They also govern compression back into lower ones.
animations: 1. Display expanding flow: 2D grid [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg] to 3D.
2. Display compressing flow: 3D object [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/object.svg] to 2D.
3. Highlight the transformation matrix as a central bridge.

sections.title: Conclusion: Why Non-Square Matters
lecture_lines: Non-square matrices are powerful mathematical engines.
They enable viewpoints, compression, and feature extraction.
Crucial for understanding modern machine learning.
animations: 1. Show a dense high-dimensional cloud of data points using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cloud.svg].
2. Display matrix transformation collapsing cloud to low-dim output.
3. Highlight classification labels appearing on the output using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/labels.svg].
